issues.title: The cutoff condition leaves the endpoint nearest image in the separated remainder

diagnostic_evidence.quote: whose support is contained in the two flat PML segments $\Sigma_{\rm pml}$ adjacent to the vertical Neumann boundaries at $x_1=\pm(L_1+d_1)$

issues.failure_explanation: The old source defines \(\Sigma_{\rm pml}=\Sigma\cap(Q_R\setminus\overline{Q_0})\), so its vertical-boundary endpoints are excluded. A fixed support contained in that open set stays a positive distance from the local boundary \(s=0\). Hence \(\mathcal B_\sigma^{\rm im}\) does not capture the nearest reflected kernel near \(s=s'=0\), and \(\mathcal E_\sigma\) retains a non-separated boundary-boundary interaction. Proposition \(\ref{prop:reflected-kernel-estimate}\) does not provide the all-boundary exponential estimate used in the proof of Lemma \(\ref{lem:Ainv-E-small}\).
issues.overall_effect: The exponential bound for the separated remainder is not established, which in turn leaves the nearest-image theorem and the main computable-BIE Neumann-series argument unsupported until the cutoff is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose the cutoff on the closed PML boundary segments so that it reaches, and is identically one in fixed neighborhoods of, the two outer endpoints s=0. With the nearest reflected interaction thereby included in the localized image operator, the existing separation and endpoint-Hankel estimates apply to the remainder and the dependent Neumann-series arguments.
issues.why_classification: The old open-set support condition is a genuine defect in the cutoff construction on which the remainder estimate relies, so it is not merely harmless notation. The repair is nevertheless short, local, routine, and already supported by the source's endpoint coordinates and endpoint-Hankel analysis; it requires no new lemma and preserves the statements, rates, and dependent convergence results.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: whose support is contained in the two flat PML segments $\overline{\Sigma_{\rm pml}}$ adjacent to the vertical Neumann boundaries at $x_1=\pm(L_1+d_1)$

issues.title: Nearest-image field estimate is stated beyond its defined and proved domain

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For \(x\) in the physical region $\Omega_p$, define the corresponding nearest-image reconstructed field by

issues.failure_explanation: The old theorem claims convergence for every compact \(K\Subset\Omega_R\). The old construction defines \(u_\sigma^{\rm ni}\) only for \(x\in\Omega_p\), and the invoked exact convergence theorem supplies the comparison with \(u\) only for compact subsets of \(\Omega_p\). Thus the proof establishes the same estimate only on \(K\Subset\Omega_p\), not throughout the PML portion of \(\Omega_R\).
issues.overall_effect: The nearest-image equation's solvability remains supported, but its field-convergence conclusion is undefined and unsupported on compact sets lying outside the physical region.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the theorem's quantifier over compact subsets of Ω_R by compact subsets of Ω_p, matching the stated domain of u_σ^{ni} and the exact field-convergence theorem used in the proof.
issues.why_classification: The old source explicitly defines the reconstructed field only on Ω_p, proves the required comparison only there, and repeatedly describes the result as physical-region convergence. Thus Ω_p is the uniquely forced well-typed reading; the Ω_R occurrence creates no coherent additional field guarantee and can be corrected without changing any argument or construction.

issues.title: The computable reconstructed field is undefined in the old notation

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and $\phi_\sigma^c$ is the unknown to be determined.

issues.failure_explanation: The old PML equations reserve \(u_\sigma\) for the exact Neumann-PML field. Equation \(\eqref{eq:appGreen-identity}\) still uses that field throughout, and the following BIE introduces only \(\phi_\sigma^c\), without defining a field \(u_\sigma^c\) or declaring \(\phi_\sigma^c\) to be its trace. The field-convergence part of the main theorem therefore contains an undefined object, although its intended reconstruction is uniquely apparent.
issues.overall_effect: The computable BIE and density remain identifiable, but the field quantity appearing in the main convergence estimate lacks a formal definition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Explicitly define the computable field by u_σ^c(x)=(SL_σ^c(g-M_βφ_σ^c))(x)-(DL_σ^cφ_σ^c)(x), and identify φ_σ^c as its boundary trace, equivalently correcting the field notation in the approximate Green representation.
issues.why_classification: The computable BIE, its unknown density, and the preceding Green representation uniquely determine the intended reconstructed field. The defect is an omitted superscript/formal definition rather than a missing mathematical inference; supplying the forced notation makes the theorem well-formed without changing its method or guarantees.

issues.title: Computable-field convergence exceeds the available physical-domain estimate

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The compact-field estimate follows directly from the exact PML-PDE convergence estimate \eqref{eq:pde-conv}.

issues.failure_explanation: The old theorem claims the computable-field estimate for every compact \(K\Subset\Omega_R\). Its proof says that this estimate follows directly from the exact PML-PDE estimate \(\eqref{eq:pde-conv}\), but that estimate is stated only for \(K\Subset\Omega_p\). No old argument extends the comparison with the physical solution through the PML part of \(\Omega_R\), so only the physical-domain conclusion is supported.
issues.overall_effect: The unique-solvability and density portions are unaffected by this root, but the main field estimate is overclaimed on compact sets in the PML region.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the computable-field estimate to compact sets K compactly contained in Ω_p. Retain the unique-solvability and density conclusions and the same physical-domain convergence rate.
issues.why_classification: Unlike an undefined expression, convergence of two fields on Ω_R is a coherent stronger scope claim, but the old proof supports it only on Ω_p. Removing the entire PML portion is a substantive yet limited domain weakening, not a merely technical exception. The resulting physical-domain theorem remains recognizably comparable and requires only a contained statement correction, so the issue is moderate rather than serious.
